messages:
alexander: quick heads-up — PR 7219 changes the microbatch scheduling heuristic (try to pack more small requests). ran the canary perf job and I'm seeing a noticeable tail bump on long-sequence workloads. can someone give a 2nd review and help decide whether we gate the rollout?

maria: on it. do you have the raw bench output or a link to the artifact? :eyes:

alexander: posted artifacts to CI, link below (perf-bench longseq1k). main numbers pasted here. the canary was run against the same model + hw as prod.

ci-bot: perf artifacts uploaded: https://ci.internal/bench/7219/longseq1k

alexander: ```
Benchmark: longseq-1k tokens (steady-state, 16 concurrency)
Old (main): p50 19.8ms | p95 182ms | p99 420ms | mem 6.1GB
New (PR 7219): p50 19.6ms | p95 205ms | p99 610ms | mem 6.4GB
Delta: p95 +12.6% | p99 +45.2% | mem +4.9%
Notes: tail increases mostly visible on sequences >800 tokens. throughput similar for short seqs.
```

sam: ouch — p99 +45% is non-trivial. do you know which part of the change likely causes the tail? scheduling bump vs kv-cache interaction?

alexander: initial suspect is the packing logic holding small requests until batch fills (a slight increase in head-of-line wait for long requests). also saw increased CPU jitter on the scheduling thread in the flamegraph. i attached the flamegraph in the artifacts.

jin: can we reproduce locally with the same synthetic load? if so we can try toggling the heuristic back to previous thresholds quickly. i can run a local canary tonight.

laura: if it's a scheduling threshold regression we should gate the rollout behind a feature flag so we can safely toggle. alexander, does PR 7219 include a flag?

alexander: added a runtime flag --enable-aggressive-packing (default true in PR). i can flip it to default false and push a patch in the branch if folks prefer a conservative rollout.

maria: please do that first. then re-run the canary; if tail goes away we know it's the packing heuristic. i'll hold my review until the new canary results. :+1:

alexander: pushed patch to set flag off by default, updated docs and test. re-triggered the perf job. link: https://ci.internal/bench/7219/longseq1k/patch

ci-bot: perf artifacts uploaded: https://ci.internal/bench/7219/longseq1k/patch

alexander: ```
Patch run (flag off)
Old (main): p99 420ms
PR 7219 (flag on): p99 610ms
PR 7219 (flag off): p99 430ms
Delta (flag off vs main): +2.4% (within noise)
```

sam: solid repro + rollback via flag. that looks safe. i'll do a code review pass for correctness and concurrency concerns tonight.

jin: i'll run an extended mem/latency burn (6h) tomorrow morning to validate no gradual buildup.

laura: once we have the extended canary green with flag off, we should merge with flag default = off and open a follow-up to experiment on the aggressive packing behind a staged rollout. that keeps prod safe.

maria: agree. if the extended run is clean i'll approve the PR and sign off on the merge window.

alexander: thanks all — i'll mark the PR with the flag-off default and add a short rollout plan in the description. cc @sam @jin for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks. ping me when the extended run completes and i'll hit approve.

laura: also add a short note to the deploy playbook about the flag to make revert fast if anything slips through.

alexander: done — playbook snippet added.

ci-bot: extended burn: https://ci.internal/bench/7219/longseq1k/extended (running, ETA ~6h)

maria: once extended completes i'll review the flamegraphs too.
